bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> as both author and committer, and its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-5wr9-m6jw-xx44 identifies the vulnerable path as TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor's Type-keyed _memberAccessors cache, GetMemberAccessorImpl constructing TypedObjectAccessor with MemberFilter/MemberRenamer, TypedObjectAccessor.PrepareMembers precomputing exposed fields/properties, and Reset not clearing the cache; it declares <= 6.6.0 affected and 7.0.0 patched. `git log -S'MemberFilter' --all --reverse -- src/Scriban src/Textamina.Scriban` makes ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d the first MemberFilter commit. `git log -L 940,940:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` traces the decisive constructor call from `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)` to `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberFilter, MemberRenamer)` at ace7a0e; its diff also adds the mutable TemplateContext.MemberFilter property and TypedObjectAccessor's _filter field/filter checks. Cache-line `git log -L 858,864:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` shows the Type-only cache predates that commit, so the large 2017 namespace move is not misclassified as the BIC. Direct parent-tree verification against c525ebfc8bfb31853da2e0280d2a24045893badb finds zero `MemberFilter` references in TemplateContext.cs and TypedObjectAccessor.cs; that tree constructs `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)`, so the advisory's filter/cache composition is absent. `git cat-file -p ace7a0e` shows one parent, human author/committer Alexandre Mutel, and no trailers, so no squash decomposition or commit-object AI signal applies. The BIC is five commits before tag v0.16.0 (`git describe --contains --tags ace7a0e` => v0.16.0~5), while its parent describes from v0.15.0; `git tag --contains ace7a0e` includes 6.6.0. Fix 8180fb6cd1f6c2727c99f8f5a745a0b991b06cfc adds `_memberAccessors.Clear()` to TemplateContext.Reset plus the stale-filter regression case. `git tag --contains 8180fb6c` begins at 7.0.0; `_memberAccessors.Clear()` is absent from tag 6.6.0 and present at src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs:982 in tag 7.0.0, matching the advisory boundary.
reasoning: The attack requires a context to first encounter a model Type under a permissive filter, causing TypedObjectAccessor to snapshot that Type's allowed members, and then to reuse the context under a stricter filter. Because lookup consults only the Type key, later member-expression access receives the old accessor and bypasses the new sandbox policy. Historical decomposition separates three stages: the Type cache existed from the initial repository history; ace7a0e was the smallest normal commit that made it security-sensitive to MemberFilter by adding the policy and feeding it into the cached accessor; 2e95889 later formalized safe TemplateContext reuse without flushing that cache. The immediate parent lacks MemberFilter and the filter-bearing constructor entirely, while ace7a0e's own diff writes both causal additions, establishing parent absence and the BIC. The direct fix clears the stale accessors during Reset and is released exactly at the declared 7.0.0 patched boundary after 6.6.0. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it is a one-parent human-authored commit with no AI marker. The correct closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI regardless of any signals on later lifecycle commits.
